event.title: Democrats Select South Carolina for First Presidential Primary in 2028
event.canonical_title: Democrats Select South Carolina for First Presidential Primary in 2028
event.summary: The Democratic National Committee has selected South Carolina to host the first primary contest for the 2028 presidential election, replacing Iowa. This decision aims to prioritize states with more diverse populations, including Nevada, which will follow South Carolina in the primary calendar. Other early voting states include New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan, and Virginia.

timeline.title: Democrats Select South Carolina for First Presidential Primary in 2028
timeline.summary: The Democratic National Committee has recommended that South Carolina hold the first presidential primary for the 2028 election cycle. This decision marks a significant shift in the primary calendar, as South Carolina will replace Iowa as the opening contest. The move aims to prioritize representation among Black and Latino voters, with Nevada also scheduled for an early primary.
key_facts: South Carolina will be the first state to hold a Democratic presidential primary in 2028.
The decision reflects a shift from Iowa to South Carolina for the opening contest.
The new primary calendar aims to prioritize Black and Latino voter representation.
